newsitem.title: USA: CASH CRUDE PRICES RANGE FIRMER, GRADES STAY STEADY.
newsitem.headline: CASH CRUDE PRICES RANGE FIRMER, GRADES STAY STEADY.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices ranged to firmer outright levels in-line with the NYMEX performance, while domestic grade barrels remained static with little action seen for September business.

Benchmark September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing pegged gains of around 15 cents mid-afternoon to $19.65-75 a barrel. Spreads between September and October WTI steadied as well, at nearly 20 cents in favor of the second month.
Grade talk put Midland/WTI at a 34-33 cents discount to September WTI, and Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James around 14-15 cents stronger than benchmark.
Sour dealings were stuck at Friday's ranges, with West Texas Sour/Midland valued at $1.50 under WTI, and Eugene Island at $1.45-38 below level.
WTI/Cushing Postings Plus barrels were at $1.87-90.

Sentiment for the short-term was based mainly on perceptions of how renewed Iraqi exports would impact the supply-demand balance. All indications point to Iraq receiving approval for oil contracts in the coming days, starting off a vigorous export schedule of some 1.5 million barrels per day.
Still, outright crude prices were watching to see the performance of unleaded gasoline heading into the brunt of the summer season.
